item.title: India’s Cockroach Janta party leader arrested amid crackdown on protests
item.description: Abhijeet Dipke was detained before planned anti-government demonstrations in Delhi The leader of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) youth movement, Abhijeet Dipke, was detained by police on Friday and then later formally arrested as authorities cracked down on fresh anti-government protests in the Indian capital. Dipke was detained before a planned Friday evening demonstration he had called in central Delhi, urging supporters of the movement to come out and hold up the Indian flag. Continue reading...

item.title: The Bundestag has debated the genocide Germany carried out in Namibia a century ago. But will it spur progress on addressing colonial crimes?
item.description: Opposition parties have forced a debate in the Bundestag on the early-20th-century genocide Germany carried out in Namibia. Will this finally spur progress in addressing colonial crimes?

item.title: Albania: Students demand political change and resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama
item.description: Empty lecture halls, burning buildings and demands for change: Albanian students are spearheading a protest movement that has become the biggest challenge to Prime Minister Edi Rama in years.

item.title: The EU wants an AI revolution. But on whose terms?
item.description: As the US and China race ahead, the European Union seeks to boost its economy with AI. Can it compete while protecting workers, safety and the climate?

item.title: Italy cuts air traffic in half amid data transmission issue
item.description: Citing problems with the data transmission network, Italian authorities have drastically reduced the volume of flights in their airspace. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.

item.title: Who was Eva Mamlok? Berlin square renamed after Jewish anti-fascist resistance fighter
item.description: She started taking action against Hitler as a teenager and never stopped until her death in a concentration camp. Berlin's Blücherplatz is now being renamed after her.

item.title: EU promotes sovereign, trusted AI as it struggles to catch US and China
item.description: At an international AI summit in Dublin, EU leaders promoted trusted and independent artificial intelligence. Critics question whether the bloc can close the gap with the US and China while maintaining strict regulation.

item.title: Formula One in Rwanda: Sportswashing claims vs. hopes for African legacy
item.description: Formula One will return to Africa for the first time since 1993. There is concern Rwanda are using it as another sportswashing opportunity, but there is also hope the event's legacy can impact wider African society.

item.title: Police raid the major pro-opposition Halk TV channel in Turkey
item.description: Turkish police raided the Istanbul headquarters of an important pro-opposition television station on Wednesdazy, the day that jailed Istanbul Mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was set to start his defense against corruption charges.

item.title: EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget
item.description: EU leaders meeting in Brussels will examine measures to curb the bloc's huge trade deficit with China. But they will also be looking to further agreement on the next EU budget ahead of some major elections next year.

item.title: Romania: 2 ships on fire in Black Sea, 7 crew missing
item.description: Two chemical tankers have caught fire in Romanian territorial waters in the Black Sea. The blazes occurred after Russian drones were sighted in Romanian airspace.

item.title: Resignation of Bärbel Bas shines light on harsh era of German politics
item.description: German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas has stepped down, citing her need to grieve a loved one and leave behind the harsh realities of government. So how did German politics get so heated?

item.title: AI-assisted dying? Doris Dörrie's new film addresses prospect of care robots
item.description: While the world debates the dangers of artificial intelligence, filmmaker Doris Dörrie explores how humanoid robots could change the way we deal with aging, caregiving and how people choose to die.

item.title: Thousands of German gamblers could sue for their money back
item.description: German gamblers may finally be able to beat the house, thanks to new court rulings in the EU and in Germany. The decisions could help gambling addicts — but the legal road might be difficult.

item.title: Germany news: Train station alcohol ban comes into force
item.description: Consuming alcohol is no longer permitted at train stations in Germany, to improve the lot of travelers and staff alike. Coalition talks are restarting in Berlin, and an inmate is loose in Essen.

item.title: Brazil's elections matter for the planet. This is why
item.description: Brazil is heading back to the polls, but the impact could be felt worldwide. With the Amazon vital to the health of the planet, the election could help shape its future.

item.title: Why Chinese tech brands are outpacing Western rivals from EVs to robot vacuums
item.description: From action cameras and smartphones to EVs and robot vacuums, Chinese brands are gaining ground worldwide, despite privacy and security concerns. What's driving their rise, and can European rivals keep up?

item.title: Manchester City, the UAE and the UK's OM in a political tangle
item.description: Nearly 20 years after arriving in England, Manchester City's UAE owners could exit amid cheating charges. That would pose a challenge for a city — and prime minister — closely tied to Abu Dhabi.

item.title: Nord Stream trial opens in Germany, defense seeks dismissal
item.description: Serhii Kuznietsov is accused of attacking civilian infrastructure in the 2022 sabotage of the Russian gas pipeline to Germany. His lawyers called Nord Stream a military target, and said their client is sworn to secrecy.

item.title: Germany's far-right AfD forges a pro-Russia alliance with the BSW
item.description: In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD and BSW are joining forces to push for negotiations with Moscow. What is driving this rapprochement?

item.title: Albania: Fire at Education Ministry as students protest
item.description: Riot police deployed in the Albanian capital Tirana on the second day of student protests. The sudden outbreak seemed at least somewhat reminiscent of the widespread demos in France courting international attention.

item.title: Trump's diesel deal with Russia is unlikely to significantly lower global fuel prices despite expectations of rapid relief
item.description: As the world's largest diesel exporter, the US benefits from high prices. At home, however, consumers are feeling the strain of rising living costs. Why Donald Trump's deal with Russia is unlikely to change that.

item.title: Nord Stream: Germany puts suspected Ukrainian pipeline saboteur on trial
item.description: A Ukrainian citizen faces court in Hamburg, accused of attacking the Nord Stream gas pipelines in 2022. It raises questions about Kyiv's possible role in the explosions. German support for Ukraine is also under scrutiny.

item.title: Fact check: Misleading graph about alleged Russian bot activity
item.description: Did attacks on Russian data centers reduce bot activity around Germany's AfD? A viral graph claims they did. But it contains significant inconsistencies and provides no evidence to support the claim.

item.title: Do non-German nationals commit more crimes than Germans?
item.description: People without German passports appear more frequently in German police crime statistics than German nationals. A new study explains why.

item.title: FIFPRO report highlights growing pains in women's football
item.description: Expected global revenue of over $1 billion and new faces at the U17 World Cup show women's football is booming, but a recent report also highlights need for better structures globally.

item.title: The hidden treasure in discarded wearable and fast tech
item.description: Sales of fast tech like mini fans and disposable e-vapes, as well as wearable health tech such as heart monitors and smartwatches are soaring. They're creating a new e-waste problem but are full of hidden treasure.

item.title: Ukraine allies in Poland after Starlink sabotage, Trump diesel deal
item.description: Germany's Johann Wadephul said hybrid plots like the Starlink fire showed Europe was "in Russia's crosshairs." The UK's Ed Miliband said Trump's Russian diesel deal led to a "very difficult few days" diplomatically.

item.title: Formula 1: Rwanda to bring sport back to Africa
item.description: The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.

item.title: Germany's China calculation shifts as import pressures eclipse export benefits
item.description: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. But rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade-defense powers to protect its industrial base.

item.title: 125 years of Thomas Mann's 'Buddenbrooks'
item.description: This over 1,000-page masterpiece offers a panoramic view of society in the 19th century and exposes the collapse of a merchant family: unrecognized sons, disillusioned daughters and the loss of middle-class ideals.

item.title: Germany: Labor Minister's resignation puts a spotlight on cracks within the government
item.description: Following the sudden resignation of Bärbel Bas as Labor Minister and co-chair of the Social Democratic Party, accusations are flying in Chancellor Merz's coalition government.

item.title: Pope lung nodule: Could it be cancer?
item.description: The case of Pope Leo shows how small lung nodules are often found during routine health checks. Quick treatment is generally advised before nodules can grow to become larger life-threatening masses.

item.title: Germany's women: Ena Mahmutovic makes her case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper
item.description: Germany's win against Australia saw Ena Mahmutovic excel in goal. The 22-year-old Bayern Munich goalkeeper is considered the successor to Ann-Katrin Berger and is making a name for herself.

item.title: How green is Europe's urban public transport? A data-driven reality check
item.description: Greener buses and cleaner fleets are reshaping public transport across Europe. But are cities moving fast enough to meet their zero-emission goals?

item.title: UK students call for school uniforms to be banned in pornography
item.description: Short skirts, knee-high socks, white blouses: Girls' school uniform items are widely used as costumes in pornographic videos. As students experience harassment, a group wants to change that.

item.title: German 'lawfare': When lawsuits become a political weapon
item.description: The Left Party is suing two government ministers for accusing them of antisemitism, while Chancellor Friedrich Merz has been sued several times by various parties. Is German politics descending into "lawfare?"

item.title: Germany's population is shrinking, but not everywhere
item.description: By 2045, Germany will have more older people, fewer workers and a smaller population overall. Yet some regions will defy this trend. Their success depends on how much they have to offer.

item.title: 'Ragebait' is the 2026 German Youth Word of the Year
item.description: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.

item.title: Operations Plan Germany: How the Bundeswehr trains for NATO collective defense
item.description: How prepared is Germany for national defense? The answer lies in the Operations Plan Germany. Military exercises such as "Red Storm Charlie" are designed to put these preparations to the test in realistic scenarios.

item.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
item.description: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

item.title: Art for freedom: Maria Kalesnikava in Bonn
item.description: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.

item.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
item.description: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?

item.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
item.description: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?

item.title: 2026 Nobel Prize winner Anne Carson: Where to start reading
item.description: The works of this year's Nobel Prize-winning poet and essayist Anne Carson can feel slightly daunting. Here are some keys to understanding her universe.

item.title: Early-onset cancer rising worldwide: Causes, risk, prevention
item.description: Across Latin America, early-onset cancer rates have risen, especially of bowel, breast and cervical cancers. But it is a worldwide trend.

item.title: Germany news: UK's Burnham visits Berlin for talks with Merz
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is visiting Berlin to launch a new bilateral treaty and hold talks with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. President Steinmeier is on a state visit to France.

item.title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited the UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
item.description: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now, the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.

item.title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
item.description: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.

item.title: German Bundeswehr: A new naval port in Emden aims to enhance Germany's defense capabilities
item.description: Citing the escalating security threat, Germany's Navy has decided to establish a second port on the North Sea coast. Emden was chosen as the location.

item.title: Gerhard Schröder visits latest Russian employer, Hyperglobus
item.description: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited a Moscow supermarket in his new role on the supervisory board. Schröder is no stranger to retirement stipends in Russia — or the scandal that accompanies them.

item.title: '90s art scene in the UK: An international, edgy trendsetter
item.description: The 1990s are remembered for Brit-pop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.

item.title: Nobel Prize in chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
item.description: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.

item.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
item.description: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

item.title: Ronaldo stays on under cloud as Messi exits internationals
item.description: Just hours before Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo posted his latest salvo in a row with Portugal. Ronaldo wants to play on despite the troubles, while Messi bathed in adulation.

item.title: Nobelitis — How winning a Nobel Prize can give you delusions of grandeur
item.description: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."

item.title: Emerging economies are embracing solar power and skipping fossil fuels much faster than Europe or the US
item.description: Renewable electricity is cheaper than ever. While the West got rich on coal and oil, some of the world's poorest countries are banking on solar, wind and water instead.

item.title: Munich up against at least six competitors for 2036 Olympics
item.description: The International Olympic Committee has revealed the six other countries intending to bid for the 2036 Olympic Games. This comes after Germany selected Munich as its Olympic candidate.

item.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant
item.description: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as its owner Skydance creates a new entertainment behemoth. Billionaire David Ellison's hostile takeover bid defeated rival efforts from Netflix.

item.title: Nobel Prize in literature: How the winner is secretly chosen
item.description: Can Xue is considered one of this year's favorites; Margaret Atwood and Salman Rushdie are other strong contenders. But what goes on behind the scenes in the selection of the Nobel Prize in literature?
